note: SR Legacy "Bananas, raw" fdc_id 173944. Expected value read out of this build's pack, which produces 89 kcal -- identical to SR Legacy's published figure. Tolerance 5%: SR Legacy is a frozen 2019 release, so nothing but a mapping regression can move this. Regex tightened to an exact match after the loose \bbananas?\b pattern matched "Puddings, banana, dry mix..." instead (lower SourceID, alphabetically first)

SR Legacy "Bananas, raw" fdc_id 173944; g-unit anchor. Build produces 22.84, matching SR Legacy's published carbohydrate-by-difference. Tolerance 5% for the same reason as the energy_kcal row above: a frozen release. Regex tightened, see that row

SR Legacy "Spinach, raw" fdc_id 168462. Build produces 2.71 mg, matching the published figure. Tolerance 5%: frozen release, well-determined mineral. Regex tightened to an exact match after the loose \bspinach\b pattern matched "Mustard spinach, (tendergreen), raw" instead (lower SourceID)

Foundation Foods "Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D"; spec anchor food; mg-unit anchor. Was 113 read off a published table; this build produces 123, so the old row was passing on the width of its band rather than on agreement. Two Foundation entries match this regex (fdc_id 322892 and 746782) and both publish calcium 123, so the lowest-SourceID tie-break cannot change the value. Tolerance 8%: Foundation Foods is re-sampled and re-released, so a refresh can move a mineral a few percent, but 8% still fails any mapping regression above that

Foundation Foods "Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D" fdc_id 322892; ug-unit anchor. Build produces 1.0; the other entry this regex matches (746782) publishes 0.96, so the 10% band holds whichever wins the lowest-SourceID tie-break. Tightened from 15% because the true value is pinned by regulation rather than by biology: US vitamin-D-fortified milk is federally standardized at ~100IU (2.5ug) per 244g cup, i.e. ~1.02ug/100g. Replaces the salmon anchor: neither salmon entry in this Foundation Foods release (fdc_id 2684440 wild caught, 2684441 farm raised) carries a vitamin_d value at all, so the golden check could never pass against it. Deliberate deviation from the design spec, which named salmon vitamin D as the anchor food

CNF "Banana, raw" food_code 1704; anchor food. Build produces 89 kcal. Tightened from 15%: the 2015 CNF release is static, and CNF carries USDA-derived figures for this food, so it agrees with the SR Legacy row exactly

CNF "Spinach, raw" food_code 2213; mg-unit anchor. Build produces 2.71 mg, the same figure SR Legacy publishes. Tightened from 30% to 10%: 10 leaves room for a CNF refresh re-analysing the mineral while still failing the kind of 15% mapping drift the wide band used to hide

CIQUAL alim_code 13005 (renamed from "banana, pulp, raw" in the 2025 release); kcal comes from const_code 328, not the kJ column. Build produces 87.6; the old expectation of 90 was read off a published table. Tolerance 8% rather than 5: CIQUAL re-issues its table every few years and computes energy from its own macro figures, so a refresh moves this more than a frozen release would

CIQUAL alim_code 13005. Build produces 19.7. CIQUAL carbohydrate is available carbohydrate, so it sits below USDA's 22.84 by-difference figure -- that gap is a definition, not an error. Tolerance 10%: available carbohydrate tracks the sugar and starch analyses, which move more across releases than energy does

CoFID 14-318; kcal column, not kJ. Build produces 81. The old row expected 95 +/-25%, a band so wide that a 15% mapping regression would have passed: 81 is what the 2021 release actually publishes, because CoFID assigns carbohydrate 3.75 kcal/g rather than 4 (its figure is monosaccharide equivalents) and gives NSP no energy at all, so its kcal runs a little under everyone else's. Tolerance 5%: CoFID is a stable, infrequently revised release. The regex is an exact match because the looser one matched 14-347, the same flesh weighed with its skin

CoFID 14-318 vitamin C. Build produces 9, not the 11 this row used to expect. Tightened from 50% to 25%, no further: 11 is the figure earlier McCance and Widdowson editions carried for this food, so a re-analysis genuinely moves ascorbic acid by close to 20% between releases and the band has to hold that. 25% still catches a unit error or a column swap

AFCD F000262. AFCD publishes kJ only; this build applies the 0.239006 factor and produces 95.36 kcal. A value near 395 means the factor was not applied. Tolerance 5%: the conversion is arithmetic on a static release, so there is nothing here to vary except the mapping

AFCD F000262 protein; g-unit anchor. Build produces 1.4 g. Tightened from 40% to 10% rather than to 5: at 1.4 g the absolute analytical scatter of a Kjeldahl determination is a large share of the value, so a re-analysis in a future AFCD release can plausibly land at 1.3 or 1.5
